description: Baseline vs specialized (few-shot) coach prompts on six fixed questions: one search per question, the same sources for both profiles, one shared generator, one greedy generation per profile.
notes: Prompt specialization only: no model weights were trained.
Both profiles use the same model, system instructions, retrieval, generation settings and token limit. The only difference is the three few-shot examples.
The few-shot examples use their own questions, which are not among the evaluation questions.
The metrics count form (words, sentences, citations). They do not measure factual accuracy. The sentence count is a heuristic.
Citations are only allowed from the sources found for the current question, never from the few-shot examples.

examples.question: What do I need to do before a duel starts?
examples.answer: Choose a difficulty, enter your secret number and press Start Duel. Vector's secret number is drawn at random only at that moment [rules-starting-a-duel].

examples.question: Can I use New Duel in the middle of a duel?
examples.answer: Yes, New Duel works during a duel and after it ends. It clears the current duel and its history but keeps the chosen difficulty [rules-new-duel].

examples.question: Do the game logs show my secret number?
examples.answer: No, the logs never contain secret numbers or full game states. A rejected round is logged only with its round number and its stage, engine or guardrail [reliability-logs].

example_messages.content:
Sources:

[rules-starting-a-duel] Starting a duel
Before the duel you choose a difficulty and enter your secret number.
Vector's secret number is drawn at random only when you press Start Duel.
During the duel the difficulty and both secret numbers do not change.
Vector's secret number is shown only after the duel ends.

Question: What do I need to do before a duel starts?
Choose a difficulty, enter your secret number and press Start Duel. Vector's secret number is drawn at random only at that moment [rules-starting-a-duel].

Sources:

[rules-new-duel] Starting over with New Duel
The New Duel button is available during a duel and after it ends. It
clears the current duel and its history and goes back to the setup. The
chosen difficulty is kept. New Duel does not change the Solo game.

Question: Can I use New Duel in the middle of a duel?
Yes, New Duel works during a duel and after it ends. It clears the current duel and its history but keeps the chosen difficulty [rules-new-duel].

Sources:

[reliability-logs] Logs without secrets
The safe service writes a log line for every round. An accepted round is
logged as duel_round_accepted with the round number and the new status. A
rejected round is logged as duel_round_rejected with the round number and
the stage, engine or guardrail. The logs never contain secret numbers or
full game states.

Question: Do the game logs show my secret number?
No, the logs never contain secret numbers or full game states. A rejected round is logged only with its round number and its stage, engine or guardrail [reliability-logs].

results.question: What happens if both players guess correctly in the same round?

sources.title: Winning and draws
sources.text:
The result is decided after both moves of a round. If both players guess
correctly in the same round, the duel is a draw. If only you guess
correctly, you win. If only Vector guesses correctly, Vector wins. If
nobody guesses correctly and the round limit is reached, the duel is a
draw. Otherwise the duel goes on to the next round.

sources.title: What the inspector checks
sources.text:
The inspector checks that the duel was still running and had rounds left,
that the settings and both secret numbers did not change, that exactly one
round was added and earlier rounds stayed the same, that both guesses are
whole numbers inside the range, that both hints match the secret numbers,
that Vector's range matches its whole history, and that the status
(playing, win or draw) is correct.

sources.title: What happens when a round is rejected
sources.text:
When a round is rejected, the game state does not change. No round is
added, the round counter stays the same, and the old duel state is kept.
A rejected guess, such as a number outside the range, shows a clear
message. A round stopped by the inspector shows only a general message,
not the inner reason, and you can simply try again.

results.question: What number range and round limit does Hard difficulty use?

sources.title: Difficulty ranges and round limits
sources.text:
The difficulty sets the range of possible numbers and the round limit.
Easy uses the numbers 1 to 20 and allows 6 rounds. Normal uses the numbers
1 to 100 and allows 8 rounds. Hard uses the numbers 1 to 50 and allows only
5 rounds. Both secret numbers and every guess must be inside the range.

sources.title: How many guesses Vector needs
sources.text:
On Easy, Vector needs at most 5 guesses, and the limit is 6 rounds, so it
always finds your number in time. On Normal, Vector needs at most 7
guesses, and the limit is 8 rounds, so it also always finds your number in
time. On Hard, the range 1 to 50 sometimes needs 6 guesses, but the limit
is only 5 rounds. So on Hard the limit of 5 rounds is not always enough
for Vector.

sources.title: Valid guesses
sources.text:
A guess must be a whole number inside the range of the difficulty. An
empty guess, text, a fraction such as 4.5, or a number outside the range
is rejected with a message. A rejected guess does not use up a round.

results.question: Does choose_guess receive the player secret number?

sources.title: What Vector's strategy sees
sources.text:
Vector's strategy only sees the bounds of its range. The function that
picks Vector's guess, choose_guess, receives only the low and high bounds.
The function that narrows the range, update_bounds, receives the bounds,
the guess and the hint. Neither function ever receives your secret number.
The game engine compares Vector's guess with your secret number to produce
the hint, like a referee.

sources.title: What Number Duel is
sources.text:
Number Duel is a two-player number guessing game. You play against Vector,
a computer opponent. Each side picks a secret number, and each side tries
to guess the other side's secret number first.

sources.text:
The inspector checks that the duel was still running and had rounds left,
that the settings and both secret numbers did not change, that exactly one
round was added and earlier rounds stayed the same, that both guesses are
whole numbers inside the range, that both hints match the secret numbers,
that Vector's range matches its whole history, and that the status
(playing, win or draw) is correct.

results.question: Does the Solo game pass through the duel inspector?

sources.title: The Solo game is not inspected
sources.text:
Only Number Duel rounds go through the inspector. The Solo game uses its
own simpler rules and does not pass through the duel inspector.

sources.title: How a duel round is accepted
sources.text:
Every duel round goes through a safe service. The game engine first builds
a candidate state for the new round. An independent inspector then checks
the step from the old state to the candidate. Only if the inspector
accepts the step is the candidate saved as the new duel state.

sources.title: Difficulty ranges and round limits
sources.text:
The difficulty sets the range of possible numbers and the round limit.
Easy uses the numbers 1 to 20 and allows 6 rounds. Normal uses the numbers
1 to 100 and allows 8 rounds. Hard uses the numbers 1 to 50 and allows only
5 rounds. Both secret numbers and every guess must be inside the range.

sources.title: Paired rounds
sources.text:
Every round has two moves, and both players always get their move. First
you guess Vector's secret number, then Vector guesses your secret number.
Vector still makes its move in a round where you already guessed right.
One round uses one attempt from the round limit.

sources.title: Valid guesses
sources.text:
A guess must be a whole number inside the range of the difficulty. An
empty guess, text, a fraction such as 4.5, or a number outside the range
is rejected with a message. A rejected guess does not use up a round.

baseline.question: Can I submit a fractional guess, and does it use a round?
baseline.answer: Yes, you can submit a fractional guess, and it does not use a round. A fractional guess is allowed, and it is rejected if it is outside the range of the difficulty. [rules-difficulty-limits]
